title: Cranberry Sauce

drivers.name: Halloween (event)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect x1.35 from 3 past Halloweens; consistent with seasonal pattern.

drivers.name: Price increase
drivers.evidence: 2.1% price hike above regular (2.85 → 2.91); no prior data on price sensitivity, but similar increases have slightly reduced demand.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween drives a strong seasonal lift (noise-adjusted x1.35), supported by 3 past occurrences. Price increased 2.1% above regular, which may dampen demand slightly. No recent promotion, so no pantry-loading effect. Supplier delivery warning introduces supply risk, but no evidence of stockouts or demand disruption. Classical model's 1.35 is a good start but overweights the event without adjusting for price. Adjust down slightly for price increase. Evidence is moderate, so shrink toward 1.0.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 9.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 20.1 | 10%-90%: 1.8 - 17.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-81% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
